title: Grapefruit & mint soy candle
subtitle: A sharp, citrus-fresh jar candle for kitchens and bathrooms
excerpt: A soy wax jar candle scented with grapefruit and peppermint essential oils. The combination gives a clean, sharp citrus note with a cool mint back, good in rooms that benefit from a freshening scent. Makes one 200 ml jar candle; burns for around 35 hours.
sourceNotes: Candle-making fundamentals: fragrance load 6-8% of wax weight for soy container candles. Pour temperature 60-65°C for container soy wax. Wick sizing: CD-12 or equivalent for a 7 cm diameter jar with soy wax; confirm with the wick manufacturer's chart for the specific jar diameter. Citrus EOs in soy candles: high vapour pressure; scent throw is modest compared to fragrance oils. Grapefruit and peppermint at a 3:1 ratio gives a dominant citrus with a clean menthol background.

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 jar candle (~200 ml; ~170 g wax fill; ~35-hour burn time)
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles and triples cleanly. Scale wax and fragrance proportionally. You'll need more pouring pitchers or a larger melting pot for larger batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Soy candles need to cure for 24-48 hours before the first burn for the best scent throw. They can be made months ahead, the cure only improves the scent.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Effectively indefinite in a cool place out of direct sunlight. The citrus scent fades after 12-18 months as the essential oils off-gas through the wax. The wax and wick remain functional beyond that.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which melted wax is poured into the container. Soy container candles pour best at 60-65°C, below this the wax sets too fast and leaves air pockets; above it the wax shrinks as it cools, leaving sinkholes.

The first burn of a new candle, long enough for the melt pool to reach the jar edge. Soy wax remembers this edge; every subsequent burn follows the same path. Burn short of the edge on the first light and the candle tunnels for its whole life.

content.text: Grapefruit and mint soy candle is a single-wick jar candle with a sharp, clean citrus scent from grapefruit essential oil and a cooling back note from peppermint. Soy wax burns slowly and evenly in a container, with a good scent throw in medium-sized rooms. One 200 ml jar; burns for around 35 hours.

items.prepNote: container-grade soy wax; melt point 48-53°C; pour at 55-60°C
5.6% of wax weight; bright citrus top note

pre-tabbed cotton wick CD-12 or equivalent for 7 cm jar diameter

content.text: Stick the wick tab to the centre of the jar base with a wick sticker or a small dab of melted wax. Loop the wick top over a wick-centring bar placed across the jar rim.

Melt the soy wax in the pouring pitcher over a simmering-water bath. Never melt wax over direct heat without watching it, wax above its flash point catches like an oil fire. Keep a fire blanket nearby. Bring to 75°C.

for container soy. Stir in the grapefruit and peppermint essential oils.
Pour into the jar in a single slow pour. Leave to set undisturbed at room temperature for at least 24 hours, soy wax sets slowly and disturbing it causes ripples and sinkholes.
Trim the wick to 5 mm before the first burn.

sets the behaviour of all subsequent burns. Burn long enough on the first light for the melt pool to reach all the way to the jar edge, in a 7 cm jar, that's around 3 hours. A short first burn leaves a wax ring around the edge that never fully melts.

Store in a cool place out of direct sunlight. The grapefruit and peppermint essential oils are high in volatile terpenes and the scent fades over 12-18 months; the candle remains functional well beyond that. The wax does not go off.
